"solution": "All digits are nonzero since 72 is nonzero, and 72 = 2^3 * 3^2. List multisets a <= b <= c <= d of digits 1..9 with product 72.

a = 1: bcd = 72. b = 1: cd = 72 gives (8,9). b = 2: cd = 36 gives (4,9), (6,6). b = 3: cd = 24 gives (3,8), (4,6). b >= 4: cd = 18 with c >= 4 is impossible. Multisets: {1,1,8,9}, {1,2,4,9}, {1,2,6,6}, {1,3,3,8}, {1,3,4,6}.

a = 2: bcd = 36 with b >= 2. b = 2: cd = 18 gives (2,9), (3,6). b = 3: cd = 12 with c >= 3 gives (3,4). b >= 4: cd = 9 with c >= 4 impossible. Multisets: {2,2,2,9}, {2,2,3,6}, {2,3,3,4}.

a = 3: bcd = 24 with b >= 3 forces cd = 8 with c >= 3, impossible. a >= 4: product >= 256.

Count arrangements: {1,1,8,9}: 4!/2! = 12; {1,2,4,9}: 24; {1,2,6,6}: 12; {1,3,3,8}: 12; {1,3,4,6}: 24; {2,2,2,9}: 4!/3! = 4; {2,2,3,6}: 12; {2,3,3,4}: 12.

Total: 12+24+12+12+24+4+12+12 = 112.",

        c+=1

"solution": "A zero digit makes the product 0 while the sum is positive, so all digits are nonzero. One digit: n = 2n forces n = 0, no solutions.

Two digits a, b: ab = 2(a+b) gives (a-2)(b-2) = 4, so (a,b) = (3,6), (4,4), (6,3): the numbers 36, 44, 63. That is 3 numbers.

Three digits, multiset a <= b <= c: abc = 2(a+b+c). If a = 1: bc = 2(1+b+c) gives (b-2)(c-2) = 6, so (b,c) = (3,8) or (4,5). If a = 2: 2bc = 2(2+b+c) gives (b-1)(c-1) = 3, so (b,c) = (2,4). If a >= 3 then abc >= 9c > 2(a+b+c). Multisets {1,3,8}, {1,4,5}, {2,2,4} give 6+6+3 = 15 numbers.

Four digits, multiset a <= b <= c <= d: abcd = 2(a+b+c+d). If a = b = 1: cd = 2(2+c+d) gives (c-2)(d-2) = 8, so (c,d) = (4,6). If a = 1, b = 2: 2cd = 2(3+c+d) gives (c-1)(d-1) = 4, so (c,d) = (2,5) or (3,3). If a = 1, b >= 3: bcd >= 9d > 2(1+b+c+d). If a = b = 2: 4cd = 2(4+c+d), i.e. 2cd = 4+c+d; with c >= 2 we have 2cd >= 4d >= 4 + c + d, with equality only when c = d = 2, giving {2,2,2,2}. If a = 2, b >= 3: 6cd > 2(2+b+c+d). Multisets {1,1,4,6}, {1,2,2,5}, {1,2,3,3}, {2,2,2,2} give 12+12+12+1 = 37 numbers.

Total: 3 + 15 + 37 = 55.",

a = 2: b + c = 13 gives (4,9), (5,8), (6,7).

a = 4: b + c = 11 with b >= 5 gives (5,6).
a >= 5: b + c <= 10 with b >= 6, c >= 7 is impossible.

"solution": "Replace each digit by its square-free part: 1, 4, 9 -> 1; 2, 8 -> 2; 3 -> 3; 5 -> 5; 7 -> 7; 6 -> 6. The product of the digits is a perfect square exactly when the product of the three square-free parts is a perfect square.

Case A: all three square-free parts equal 1. Each digit is 1, 4 or 9: 3^3 = 27 numbers.
